title: Check yourself: Polling, results and retries

questions.stem: The first line of a result file carries the id of the request sent third. What should the program do?

options.text: Treat the file as corrupt, since entries must follow the order of submission
options.says: Ruled out because the file "may not match the ordering of requests when the batch was created".

options.text: Pair every entry with its source through the label you assigned, as the order is arbitrary
options.says: The page says "always use the `custom_id` field" to match, since the file order carries no meaning.

options.text: Sort by finishing time, since that is the order that counts for the match
options.says: Ruled out because the page names the match key: "always use the `custom_id` field".

options.text: Match by position once the first entries are read, since the rest follow suit
options.says: Ruled out because "Batch results can be returned in any order".

questions.stem: A batch ends with 900 succeeded results, 50 errored, 30 canceled and 20 expired. Which results are billed?

options.text: The 900 and the 20 that timed out, as those had reached a queue
options.says: Ruled out because an expired request means "the 24 hours passed before this request was sent", so it never ran.

options.text: The 900 and the 50 that failed on an error, as both ran a model
options.says: Ruled out because "You will not be billed for these requests." is stated for the errored results too.

options.text: All 1,000, as the discount is a flat half of the total
options.says: Ruled out because "Only the `succeeded` results carry tokens that are billed."

options.text: The 900 that worked, as the other three kinds carry no charge
options.says: The page says "You will not be billed for these requests." of the three failure types.

questions.stem: A result line for one request shows an error of type invalid_request_error. What is the sound next step?

options.text: Resubmit it unchanged, since a failure is usually a one-off
options.says: Ruled out because of "fix it first; the same request fails again".

options.text: Correct the body, then send it in a later batch
options.says: The page's table says for this error "fix it first; the same request fails again", and then a new batch can carry it.

options.text: Wait for the same batch to retry it, since that is automatic
options.says: Ruled out because "once a batch has been submitted, it cannot be modified", so a batch does not retry on its own.

options.text: Drop it, since an errored entry cannot join a new batch
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "Collect the failures into a new, smaller batch."
